title: Validation of a real-time PCR panel for detection of canine respiratory pathogens
author: Dong, Tsui, et al.
materials: Detailed information for clinical sample collection and nucleic acid extraction were provided in Dong et al., 2022 [4]. As described, a total of 740 canine clinical samples were used for diagnostic validation of the new assay. Nucleic acids were extracted by MagMax™ Viral/Pathogen Nucleic Acid Isolation Kit (Applied Biosystems/ThermoFisher, Foster City, CA, USA) according to the manufacturer's recommendations. Extracted nucleic acids were tested with the newly developed CIRD panel RT-PCR assay, and compared with an older version of the panel test that detects the same pathogens, except that it does not differentiate M. cynos from M. canis.

For quantification purposes, a fragment encompassing the RT-qPCR primer binding region for eight of the nine pathogen targets was amplified from clinical samples using the sequencing primers listed in Table 2 of Dong et al., 2022 [4]. Amplified fragments were cloned and used as positive amplification controls. We did not have a B. brochiseptica positive sample in the beginning of the project, and the target was synthesized and cloned. Insert sequences of all nine plasmids were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Plasmids were extracted using the Qiagen QIAamp plasmid mini kit. Plasmid DNA concentration was measured using a Nanodrop (ThermoFisher) spectrophotometer. RNA templates for the four RNA viruses, CPIV, CDV, CIA, and CRCoV, were also synthesized using MEGAscript T7 Transcription Kit, and purified with MEGAclear Kit (Invitrogen/ThermoFisher, Waltham, MA).

steps.title: Collect canine respiratory samples
steps.instruction: Obtain a total of 740 canine clinical respiratory samples (nasal swabs and lung tissues) as described in Dong et al., 2022 and record each sample for later analysis.

steps.title: Extract nucleic acids with MagMax kit
steps.instruction: Extract nucleic acids from all 740 samples using the MagMax™ Viral/Pathogen Nucleic Acid Isolation Kit (Applied Biosystems/ThermoFisher) following the manufacturer’s recommended protocol.

steps.title: Run CIRD panel RT‑PCR assay
steps.instruction: Test the extracted nucleic acids with the newly developed CIRD panel real‑time PCR assay; optionally compare results with the older version of the panel that does not differentiate M. cynos from M. canis.

steps.title: Prepare positive‑control plasmids and RNA templates
steps.instruction: Generate quantitative positive controls for the panel:

substeps.instruction: Amplify a fragment covering the RT‑qPCR primer‑binding region for eight of the nine pathogen targets from clinical samples using the sequencing primers listed in Table 2 of Dong et al., 2022.
Clone each amplified fragment into a plasmid vector; for B. bronchiseptica, synthesize the target sequence and clone it directly.
Confirm the insert sequences of all nine plasmids by Sanger sequencing.
Extract plasmid DNA with the Qiagen QIAamp Plasmid Mini Kit.
Measure plasmid DNA concentration using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer (ThermoFisher).
Synthesize RNA templates for the four RNA viruses (CPIV, CDV, CIA, CRCoV) using the MEGAscript T7 Transcription Kit.
Purify the transcribed RNA with the MEGAclear Kit (Invitrogen/ThermoFisher).

steps.title: Validate high‑concentration target effect (CDV spiking)
steps.instruction: Assess whether a high‑concentration CDV target influences detection of other pathogens in the same reaction:

substeps.instruction: Select a diagnostic sample that tested CDV‑positive with a low Ct value (Ct = 19).
Prepare three CDV template concentrations: the original undiluted sample and two 100‑fold serial dilutions.

Spike each CDV concentration into four diagnostic samples as follows: (i) a sample positive for both CIV and CRCoV, (ii) a sample positive for CIV only, (iii) a sample positive for CRCoV only, and (iv) a sample negative for both CIV and CRCoV.
Run Subpanel 3 of the CIRD PCR panel on all spiked reactions.
Record Ct values and calculate standard deviations and coefficients of variation (expected 0.44–0.84 SD and 1.38 %–2.72 % CV).

steps.title: Validate sample‑type effect (nasal vs lung spiking)
steps.instruction: Determine whether nasal swab and lung tissue matrices affect assay sensitivity:

substeps.instruction: Prepare three concentrations of each positive‑control plasmid DNA (for DNA targets) and each in‑vitro‑transcribed RNA (for RNA targets).
Spike each concentration into separate all‑target‑negative nasal swab samples and into separate all‑target‑negative lung tissue samples.
Extract nucleic acids from all spiked samples using the same MagMax™ Viral/Pathogen Nucleic Acid Isolation Kit protocol.
Test the extracted nucleic acids with the full CIRD panel PCR assay.
Compare Ct values, standard deviations, and coefficients of variation between nasal and lung matrices (differences should be minor).
